This is equivalent to finding the supremum of the minimum absolute row/column sums. Let M be this supremum. For a matrix to have all |Ri| > M and |Cj| > M, let k be the number of row sums in the upper interval ((M+n)/2, n] and p be the number of column sums in the same. The conditions for existence are k < n^2/(M+n), p < n^2/(M+n), k > (n-M)/2, and k(M+n) < 2pk + (n-p)(n-M). Maximizing M subject to these over integers k, p yields M = 13638/59.
